penalties_applied.name: regulated_industry
penalties_applied.reason: Financial services (banks, trading desks, hedge funds) are heavily regulated; any AI tooling sold to them must navigate FINRA, SEC, MiFID II, and internal compliance review cycles that require enterprise legal/sales resources far beyond a solo operator.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Enterprise financial institution sales require live demos, security reviews, procurement cycles of 6–18 months, and executive sign-off — this cannot be async or self-serve.

penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Deploying a compliant on-prem or VPC-deployed AI layer for a financial institution requires bespoke infrastructure scoping, security questionnaire responses, penetration testing coordination, and ongoing customer success — all human-intensive.

rationale: The pain is real and the willingness-to-pay is exceptionally strong — Goldman-tier institutions would genuinely pay large sums for a compliant AI layer — but this is not a solo non-technical operator opportunity at any realistic near-term horizon. Buyers are enterprise compliance and IT leadership at major financial institutions, and the sales cycle alone (security review, legal sign-off, procurement) takes 6–18 months and requires a dedicated enterprise sales team plus deep compliance expertise. Buildability is very low: a VPC-deployed, audit-logged AI system with data-residency guarantees and financial-grade security controls is a multi-engineer infrastructure product, not a Claude prompt plus a landing page. The penalties for regulated industry, synchronous human sales, and human-intensive fulfillment correctly collapse the score to drop territory. This opportunity is real for a well-funded team; it is the wrong opportunity for this factory.
solution_plan: This opportunity should not be pursued by this factory. The buyer (enterprise financial institution compliance/IT leadership) requires in-person relationship-building, responds only to vendors with established compliance credentials, and the product itself (on-prem/VPC AI with audit trails, data-residency, SOC 2 Type II, potentially FedRAMP) is a multi-year infrastructure build requiring a full engineering team. A solo non-technical operator using Claude and a Stripe link cannot build, sell, or maintain this — attempting it would produce no revenue and significant wasted effort. If Youval has a direct relationship with a compliance officer at a mid-market financial firm who would co-design and champion this internally, that changes the calculus, but as a cold-start opportunity it is a drop.
notes: Failing build_gates: buildability_with_ai (scored 2, floor 6), operational_autonomy (scored 2, floor 7), willingness_to_pay passes (8) but the other structural problems override. Regulated industry penalty applied. Total collapses to 1.4 — well below the validate threshold of 5.5.
